violations.text: Soap and paper towels were not available at the hand-washing sink in the pantry for front of house. Hand-washing sinks must be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap and a hand drying provision. Soap and paper towels were provided during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

Raw animal foods (such as fish filets) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as prepared sauces) in the prep unit #1. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Food items were rearranged during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

Rice and Pasta was observed at temperatures ranging from 66-70 degrees Fahrenheit in the kitchen prep unit for service. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Per PIC, the food items had just been prepared and placed into the prep unit for service. Food items were moved to other refrigeration to finish the cooling process. Food items must be 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below prior to service. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

The consumer advisory provided does not disclose the foods on the menu that are raw or undercooked. Whole intact beef and hamburgers are served raw or undercooked to the customer's request. Establishment is to add an indicating symbol signifying which items are served raw or undercooked to the consumer's request. New Violation. Correct By: 10/20/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Per interview of pasta and rice were placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Food items were placed onto sheet trays to finish cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

Raw shrimp was observed thawing on the counter in stagnant water. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must be thawed in one of the following manners: under refrigeration (41 degrees Fahrenheit or less); completely submerged under running water; as part of the cooking process; or in the microwave if cooked immediately after thawing. Food items were still partially frozen and were placing into the food prep sink with running water to finish the thawing process. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

The presence of small flies is not controlled as evidenced by live activity in the pantry. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. Establishment is to work with pest control to create an action plan to obtain control of pest presence. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

A glue type insect control device was observed hung over the soiled and clean portions of ware washing area including the storage area of sanitized dishes. Insect control devices shall be installed so that the devices are not located over a food preparation area; and food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Insect control devices were removed during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

Bowls are being used as scoops in containers of various dry ingredients. Utensils used to dispense non-time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods such as sugar and flour must be stored in the food item with their handles above the top of the food within the container. Bowls were removed during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the 1-door low boy and dishwasher in the pantry have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. New Violation. Correct By: 10/08/2026
The drip line from the soda gun, was observed draining onto the floor in the Bellevue bar. PIC placed the drip line back into the drain. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/06/2026

The floors and walls throughout the pantry have an accumulation of soil residue and/or food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 10/08/2026

Pulled pork, which was prepared in advance, was not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. Food items were prepared on 12/14 and were observed at 54 degrees Fahrenheit in the walk-in cooler. Food items were voluntarily disposed of during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/15/2025

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Per interview of staff, pulled pork was placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Proper cooling methods guidance was provided during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/15/2025

The door to the outside, located in the back, is not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. Per PIC, new door is ordered and will arrive and be installed on December 22nd or 23rd. New Violation. Correct By: 12/26/2025
The hand-washing sink in the kitchen by the dish area was lacking paper towels. Paper towels were provided during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/09/2025

Raw animal foods (stuffed shrimp) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (gravy and french onion soup) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/09/2025

The kitchen walk-in cooler was observed held at an ambient temperature of 47 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items were evaluated during the time of inspection and voluntarily disposed of during the time of inspection. Service arrived during the time of inspection New Violation. Correct By: 12/09/2025

Cooked lobster meat was observed thawed within their original reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Seafood items must be removed from ROP packaging prior to thawing to allow the reintroduction of oxygen into food item. ROP cooked lobster meat were observed at 39-40 degrees Fahrenheit and were voluntarily disposed of during time of inspection. Guidance was provided during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/09/2025

The door to the outside, located in the back, is not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 12/26/2025

The doors to the outside, located at both front entry doors and the kitchen, are not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 03/01/2025
Refrigerator door gaskets were observed in poor repair on both prep units and all low boy units. Refrigerator door gaskets must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 03/01/2025

A hose is connected to the faucet at the prep sink. This faucet is lacking a backflow prevention device. An approved backflow prevention device is required in order to prevent backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply at each point of use at a food establishment. Hose was removed from faucet during time of inspection. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 02/10/2025

An employee was observed touching ready to eat food (lettuce) with bare hands. Food employees must not touch exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, single use gloves, or dispensing equipment. Contaminated food items were voluntarily disposed of during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 01/30/2025

The hand-washing sink in the service area was blocked by a strainer within the sink basin, and staff was also observed dumping liquids into hand sink. A hand-washing sink shall be accessible at all times for employee use. Strainer was removed from sink basin during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 01/30/2025

The chlorine sanitizer concentration for the sanitizing cycle of the glass washer in the pantry was 0 parts per million (ppm). Chlorine sanitizing solutions must be between 50-100 ppm. Chemical sanitizer bottle was observed empty and once replaced unit was unable to achieve a prime on sanitizer to function properly. Establishment is to send glasses and other dishes to main dishwashing area in kitchen until unit is repaired. Call for service was placed during time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 01/30/2025

Raw tuna, seabass, and cooked lobster meat was observed thawed within their original reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Seafood items must be removed from ROP packaging prior to thawing to allow the reintroduction of oxygen into food item. ROP seabass and cooked lobster meat were observed at 37-38 degrees Fahrenheit and were removed from packaging during time of inspection. ROP raw tuna was observed at temperatures ranging from 40-41 degrees Fahrenheit and were voluntarily disposed of during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 01/30/2025

The doors to the outside, located at both front entry doors and the kitchen, are not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 03/01/2025
Refrigerator door gaskets were observed in poor repair on both prep units and all low boy units. Refrigerator door gaskets must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 03/01/2025

A hose is connected to the faucet at the prep sink. This faucet is lacking a backflow prevention device. An approved backflow prevention device is required in order to prevent backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply at each point of use at a food establishment. Hose was removed from faucet during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 01/30/2025
